pumac-2011-finals-b-01.prompt: If the plane is partitioned into a grid of congruent equilateral triangles, prove that there does not exist a square with vertices at the vertices of this grid.
pumac-2011-finals-b-01.answer: Place the grid at $\{m(1,0)+n(\tfrac12,\tfrac{\sqrt3}2)\}$; a $90^\circ$ rotation of a lattice vector is never a lattice vector because $\sqrt3$ is irrational
pumac-2011-finals-b-01.reviewNote: No official solution or answer key is published for the finals; the proof was written and checked independently.

pumac-2011-finals-b-02.prompt: Prove for irrational number $\alpha$ and positive integer $n$ that $$\left(\alpha+\sqrt{\alpha^2-1}\right)^{1/n}+\left(\alpha-\sqrt{\alpha^2-1}\right)^{1/n}$$ is irrational.
pumac-2011-finals-b-02.answer: With $u,v$ the two $n$-th roots, $uv=1$, so $u^k+v^k$ is an integer polynomial in $S=u+v$; if $S$ were rational then $2\alpha=u^n+v^n$ would be rational
pumac-2011-finals-b-02.reviewNote: No official solution or answer key is published for the finals; the proof was written and checked independently.

pumac-2011-finals-b-03.prompt: In a $k$-player tournament for $k>1$, every player plays every other player exactly once. Find with proof the smallest value of $k$ such that it is possible that for any two players, there was a third player who beat both of them.
pumac-2011-finals-b-03.answer: $k=7$ (each player must lose at least $3$ games, forcing $\binom k2\ge3k$; and $i$ beats $i+1,i+2,i+4 \pmod 7$ works)
